title: Alert fatigue: what deserves to wake someone, and what only deserves a log line

videos.script: At eight minutes to five on the thirtieth, Rafa's phone buzzed. Card provider, slow again. {{buzz}} That alert paged sixteen times that quarter. Three times, it mattered. {{sixteen}} So he acknowledged it, and went back to work. Twenty-eight minutes later the retry started charging shops twice. {{twice}} Nobody blames him. The team had taught him that this page could wait, one false alarm at a time. {{taught}} This lesson is about alert fatigue. What deserves to wake somebody, and what only deserves a log line. {{deserves}} How to count which alerts are worth it. And how a team gets back to the only pager worth carrying: one that people believe. {{believe}}
